data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Ced was a name given to the beautiful youths who tended to the groves of the Cedar tree. They were renowned for their strength and grace. In Christianity, Ced is considered a variation of the name Cedric, which means 'powerful ruler'. The name Ced carries the meaning “Handsome, beautiful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ced usually hope their child will grow to embody handsome, beautiful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ced total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Ced
in_english.meaning: a variant of Cedric, derived from the Old English words 'cēd' and 'rīc', meaning 'bounty' and 'ruler'
in_english.long_meaning: Ced is a variant of the name Cedric, which is derived from the Old English words ‘cəd’ and ‘rıc’, meaning ‘bounty’ and ‘ruler’. In Christian tradition, the name Cedric is associated with the concept of generosity and leadership, reflecting the qualities of a benevolent ruler. As a given name, Cedric has been popularized in literature, particularly in the works of Sir Walter Scott, who featured a character by that name in his novel Ivanhoe. In modern times, the name Cedric has been adapted and shortened to Ced, which has become a distinct and handsome name in its own right.
